authority: Operator-confirmed design (grilling completed in the prior session; this entry is its durable Tier-4 record). Application of already-ratified rules (C2 §17.5.3, C3 §16.5); NOT a constitutional amendment.
ticket: CHK-1 (plans/tickets_phase8_review.md §2). First acceptance criterion mandated a /grilling session before implementation; this entry records its outcome so the design no longer lives only in the (non-Tier-4) handoff.
trigger: Phase-scoped runs (--phase 8) bootstrap phases 1-7 from a prior run's durable gate evidence (runner/dag_scheduler.py bootstrap_phase_prerequisites), so those gate results legitimately carry a PRIOR run_id. The checkpoint-publish skill's Step 2 hard-fails on that run_id mismatch (MALFORMED_ARTIFACT), blocking n08f_revision. Gate evaluation itself already tolerates the mismatch via runner/predicates/gate_pass_predicates.py _check_continuation_acceptance; the skill's own check was the sole remaining blocker. In a --phase 8 run the 6 confirmed gates split into gate_09_budget_consistency (phase 7, bootstrapped -> prior run_id) and gate_10a/b/c/d + gate_11 (phase 8, current run_id); only the cross-run ones need provenance.
finding: Every step of .claude/skills/checkpoint-publish.md is a deterministic transform of its inputs (existing-checkpoint guard = file-exists + status lookup; gate validation = presence/schema_id/status/run_id equality checks; Tier-3 snapshot = data.get; write = fixed gate-id list). No inference, no domain reasoning; only published_at is non-deterministic (a publication stamp, like gate_result.evaluated_at). Modelling it as a Claude skill was the anti-pattern. This is precisely the C2 (§17.5.3) deterministic-component pattern.

decisions.D1_authorization: A cross-run run_id is authorized at publish time by DETERMINISTIC set-membership against accepted_upstream_gates (the record bootstrap_phase_prerequisites writes to the run manifest). The provenance quad is assembled by a deterministic component and recorded via the inherited_artifacts idiom. Claude makes NO provenance judgment.
decisions.D2_composition: Option 2 - RETIRE checkpoint-publish as a skill. It is 100% mechanical (see finding). A single deterministic component (runner/checkpoint_publisher.py, id 'checkpoint_publisher') writes the WHOLE checkpoint including the authorized quad. No companion artifact, no Claude in the provenance path. The operator explicitly accepted shedding the ~370 lines of skill-spec tests (tests/runner/test_checkpoint_publish_spec.py) as debt.
decisions.D3_schema_version: KEEP orch.checkpoints.phase8_checkpoint.v1. inherited_gate_provenance is optional/additive (absent for all-current-run checkpoints), exactly as inherited_artifacts was added to gate_result with no schema bump. No migration; an existing all-current-run checkpoint stays byte-identical and valid.
decisions.D4_reader_strictness: gate_12's checkpoint_published predicate is CONSISTENCY-ONLY and records the fingerprint. It re-validates the quad against durable gate results (evidence_path exists, is a passing gate_result, run_id == original_run_id, input_fingerprint matches, versions match) and fails closed on drift or hidden inheritance (a confirmed gate whose durable run_id differs from the checkpoint's with no quad entry). It does NOT recompute input_fingerprint from current inputs - that content-freshness step belongs to ST-1 (a separate ticket). The checked fingerprint is recorded durably (in the gate_12 result via predicate details) so ST-1 can build on it.

threat_model_boundary: The quad closes the SILENT provenance-loss path - a durable checkpoint asserting inherited gates as its own run's product. It gives internal consistency + auditability against durable Tier-4 evidence. It is NOT tamper-proofing against a malicious docs/ writer - that is out of scope, identical to every other Tier-4 artifact (anyone with docs/ write access can fabricate). 'Self-validating without .claude/runs/' means the checkpoint + durable gate results are internally consistent and traceable; run-time entitlement to inherit (the freshness decision made at bootstrap) is inherently not re-derivable from cleared state and is not claimed to be.
no_constitutional_amendment_rationale: Retiring one skill and moving checkpoint publication to a deterministic component is a straight APPLICATION of already-ratified rules - C2 (§17.5.3: components read declared inputs and write canonical artifacts) and C3 (§16.5: manifest-bound components). Nothing in the constitution mandates that checkpoint publication be a skill. §17.6.2 (components cannot evaluate gates) is respected: the component writes the checkpoint; the SCHEDULER still evaluates gate_12. §17.6.4 (skills do not invoke skills) is not applicable. §17.6.3 (gate results written exclusively by the gate evaluator) is untouched: a checkpoint is not a gate result. Recorded here per §14.1 so a future reader does not mistake this for an un-recorded constitutional change.
